title: Credit Controller
description:
About the Role
We're looking for an experienced Credit Controller to join our Finance team and take ownership of the debtor portfolio and cash collection process. This is a hands-on role suited to someone who's comfortable managing customer relationships as well as the numbers: chasing payments by phone and email in a professional and courteous manner, resolving billing queries, and keeping debtor days on track.

You'll work closely with the finance function, including invoicing and management reporting, as well as the wider business, and play a key part in protecting cash flow across the business.

We're ideally looking for someone motivated and excited to take ownership, improve credit control processes, and make an impact in a fast-paced, growing business.

- Take ownership of the debtor portfolio, managing the credit control and cash collection process to ensure prompt payment of invoices

- Investigate and resolve invoice queries and disputes in a timely manner, liaising with sales, account management and operations teams as needed

- Credit control experience, ideally in a SaaS business
- Excellent spoken and strong written communication skills
- Ability to build customer and stakeholder relationships
- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
- Computer proficiency, ideally with advanced Excel skills; experience with accounting software is a bonus but training will be given

- Strong organisational and prioritisation skills with excellent attention to detail
- Proactive, self-motivated and driven, ability to problem solve and work independently

title: Business Administrator
description: Join our dedicated Adult Community Mental Health Team and make a real difference every day. We are seeking an exceptional Administrator to lead our administrative service, ensuring patients, clinicians and managers receive the high-quality support they need. This is a varied, rewarding and influential role within a friendly and supportive team. Based in Newton Abbot, the 30-hour post can be worked across either 4 or 5 days. This is an exciting opportunity to lead and develop the administrative service for our busy Adult Community Mental Health Team based at Estuary House. Our Business Administrator plays a key role in supporting patients, clinicians and managers, helping to ensure the delivery of a responsive, high-quality service alongside keen and engaged colleagues. You will lead a dedicated team of administrators in a positive and supportive environment where staff feel valued, motivated and empowered to succeed. Responsibilities include line management, recruitment, staff development and maintaining high standards of performance and service delivery. Working closely with the Clinical Team Manager, you will help drive continuous improvement by developing and refining systems and processes that enable clinicians to work efficiently and maximise the time they spend supporting patients. You will promote effective communication, collaboration and problem-solving across the team. The role includes minuting meetings, maintaining staffing and patient systems, ensuring compliance with Trust standards and fostering a culture of teamwork and engagement. description: Join Our Dynamic Team at Exeter Liaison Psychiatry! Are you ready to be part of a team that truly values, supports and invests in its staff? We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Administrator to join the Exeter Liaison Psychiatry team at Wonford House! We are on the lookout for an enthusiastic and highly motivated individual with exceptional IT, communication and organisational skills, with an eye for detail in typing patient assessment letters. Your contribution will be invaluable and we will support you in developing the skills you need to thrive. Why Join Us? Exciting and varied role in a supportive team Professional development opportunities Fast-paced, rewarding environment where your work truly makes a difference! Flexible working pattern to be discussed during the appointment process. Interview date: 20 October 2026 . You will be supporting a multi-disciplinary team that includes Consultants, Junior Doctors, Psychologists, Nurses, Social Workers, Occupational Therapists, Healthcare Assistants and of course, our amazing Administrative team! title: Medical Administrator
description: Job summary Devon Square Surgery is seeking a Medical Administrator to join our team of dedicated, patient-focused professionals. A comprehensive training package is provided for new employees. Working hours will be fixed across between 3 to 5 days depending on full or part time requirement, and will include either one early or one late shift. In addition, flexibility in working hours will be required to work to cover staff absences/leave occasionally. Applicants must have excellent customer service, administration, and IT skills. A systematic and accurate approach to clerical work is also essential for this role. The main duties of the role are to: Provide a professional, warm, and friendly reception and phone manner that is sensitive to patient circumstances. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence. Demonstrate excellent verbal communication and interpersonal skills. Present a professional and smart appearance to patients. Use own initiative and prioritise workloads according to patient and practice needs. Employees will be required to: Carry out administrative tasks relating to patient records, including: filing, document management, facilitating patient access and processing new prescriptions. Scan and code incoming clinical correspondence. Take actions where appropriate, including forwarding to relevant clinicians for action if required. Ensure repeat prescriptions are generated accurately and efficiently within 48 hours, as specified by the practice. Take action as directed by other team members. Follow practice protocols to ensure consistent and high-quality care is provided to patients. Process surgery correspondence (paper and electronic), linking to patient records and maintaining a healthcare audit chain. Schedule appointments on the practice system, processing requests for “on the day” and pre-bookable appointments from patients – face to face and on the telephone. Ensure that all visitors and telephone callers to the practice are greeted professionally, and their requirements managed appropriately. Manage the flow of patients arriving at the reception desk for appointments, prescriptions or queries. Ensure pathology lab samples are correctly labelled and handled appropriately Maintain workplace infection prevention and control measures.

title: Business Support Administrator
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a business support administrator to join a project which is launching a centralised administration hub coordinating physical health monitoring activities across Devon. This will include holding central records of all patients who require physical health monitoring whatever service is supporting them, booking appointments, managing DNAs and liaising with teams across the directorate. We are seeking an enthusiastic administrator with excellent IT, communication, and organisational skills. The role offers the opportunity for hybrid working. You will get job satisfaction in helping colleagues and patients efficiently and compassionately. You will be supported and trained to reach your professional best, with opportunities for continuing development, training and career progression. There's lots more to working at Devon Partnership Trust - if you would like to apply or find out more, please get in touch. Working as part of a small team, you will be involved in all aspects of the appointment booking process and follow up administration: Booking initial appointment slots within the clinic or community setting Managing waiting lists to book follow up appointments Managing cancellations and non-attendance Handling queries from patients and referrers Supporting clinical staff with managing clinics and caseloads About you You will have experience of working in a team, providing administrative support in an office environment. The role involves communication, so we expect that you have excellent verbal and written skills. We expect you to have a working knowledge of Microsoft Office packages and be comfortable with working with electronic records. Interacting with patients and the public you will be confident in giving non-clinical information and advice that improves their experience. Dealing with sensitive information daily, you will understand the importance of data security. You will often work under pressure and without direct supervision, so we are looking for someone confident and capable. You will prioritise tasks, and manage your own workload, providing support for your colleagues where required. You will become an important part of the team, working to ensure that every patient receives high quality care.
